cases.note: GAP: error_reset()/clear() leave the lightweight error object valid, and the compiler tracks no reset-state, so a stale-state misuse compiles cleanly (check rc=0, build rc=0, no [CPLUS- diagnostic]). The pattern is memory-safe here because reset clears fields; cover stale-state expectations in a runtime/behavioral test.

Heap error slot released with cplus_release() then read via slot->failed. Both commands fail with [CPLUS-LIFETIME] [CPLUS-SAFE-LIFETIME] use-after-free: member access through released pointer. Residual gap: method-call sugar on a released error* lowers to a free function call and is NOT checked (probe: cplus_release(e); e->ok() compiles).

error_reset(NULL) is contract-valid, but dereferencing a null error* via slot->failed is contract-invalid. Both commands fail with [CPLUS-LIFETIME] [CPLUS-SAFE-LIFETIME] null pointer dereference. Residual gap: method calls on a null error* (e.g. e->ok()) lower to free function calls and are NOT caught; direct member access is.
